git-alias-pos.label: pos
git-alias-pos.rubric: When resolving CamelCased aliases in early config, names must match config keys case-insensitively; -h output is independent.
allowed_old: alias: use the early config machinery to expand aliases

Instead of discovering the .git/ directory, reading the config and then
trying to painstakingly reset all the global state if we did not find a
matching alias, let's use the early config machinery instead.
allowed_new:
It is totally legitimate to add CamelCased aliases, but due to the way
config keys are compared, the case does not matter.

Therefore, we must compare the alias name insensitively to the config
keys.

git-cvs-pos.label: pos
git-cvs-pos.rubric: When neither CLI nor .cvspass supplies a password, initialize the scrambled empty value to A; object IDs do not change password handling.
allowed_old: Do not scramble password read from .cvspass

Passwords stored in .cvspass are already scrambled, we do not
want to scramble them twice. Only passwords read from the
command line are scrambled.
allowed_new:
If we do not read a password from the command line, and there are no
passwords stored in .cvspass, we have to initialize the password with
just "A".

that had the safety.

git-trash-pos.label: pos
git-trash-pos.rubric: The output directory inherited/defaulted by the subtests puts their scratch outside t0000; set TEST_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY for the sub-tests. Indentation does not affect it.
allowed_old:
After the location of $TRASH_DIRECTORY is adjusted by
$TEST_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY, we go on to use the $test variable to make the
trash directory and cd into it.  This means that when
$TEST_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY is not "." and an absolute --root has not been
specified, we do not remove the trash directory once the tests are
complete (remove_trash is set to $TRASH_DIRECTORY).
Fix this by always referring to the trash directory as $TRASH_DIRECTORY.
allowed_new:
These scratch areas for sub-tests should be under the t0000 trash
directory, but because TEST_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY defaults to
TEST_DIRECTORY, which is exported to help sub-tests find
test-lib.sh, the sub-test trash directories are created under the
toplevel t/ directory instead.  Because some of the sub-tests
simulate failures, their trash directories are kept around.

Fix it by explicitly setting TEST_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY appropriately for
sub-tests.

cross-trash.label: neg
cross-trash.rubric: Distinct historical decision. The output directory inherited/defaulted by the subtests puts their scratch outside t0000; set TEST_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY for the sub-tests. Indentation does not affect it.

git-trash-neg.label: neg
git-trash-neg.rubric: The output directory inherited/defaulted by the subtests puts their scratch outside t0000; set TEST_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY for the sub-tests. Indentation does not affect it.
allowed_old:

git-symlink-pos.label: pos
git-symlink-pos.rubric: Canonicalizing an absolute worktree symlink dereferences the link, making Git act on the target instead of the link. Local clone object-store symlinks are a different operation.
allowed_old: setup: translate symlinks in filename when using absolute paths
allowed_new:
When symlinks in the working tree are manipulated using the absolute
path, git dereferences them, and tries to manipulate the link target
instead.

This is a regression introduced by 18e051a:
  setup: translate symlinks in filename when using absolute paths
(which did not take symlinks inside the work tree into consideration).

cross-symlink.label: neg
cross-symlink.rubric: Distinct historical decision. Canonicalizing an absolute worktree symlink dereferences the link, making Git act on the target instead of the link. Local clone object-store symlinks are a different operation.

git-am-pos.label: pos
git-am-pos.rubric: Patch-format detection must ignore leading whitespace that webmail prepends to saved mail. Resuming a failed patch without a tty is independent.
allowed_old:
Default to mbox format if input is from stdin. Otherwise, look at the
first few lines of the first patch to try to guess its format.
allowed_new:
Some web-based email clients prepend whitespace to raw message
transcripts to workaround content-sniffing in some browsers.  Adjust
the patch format detection logic to ignore leading whitespace.

cross-am.label: neg
cross-am.rubric: Distinct historical decision. Patch-format detection must ignore leading whitespace that webmail prepends to saved mail. Resuming a failed patch without a tty is independent.

development-checkout.label: pos
development-checkout.rubric: Initial checkout requires updating the worktree and index; cheap test ordering is incidental.
allowed_old:
Skip merging the commit, updating the index and working directory if and
only if we are creating a new branch via "git checkout -b <new_branch>."
Any other checkout options will still go through the former code path.
allowed_new:
When doing a 'checkout -b' do a full checkout including updating the working
tree when doing the initial checkout. As the new test involves an filesystem
access, do it later in the sequence to give chance to other cheaper tests to
leave early. This fixes the regression in behavior caused by fa655d8411
(checkout: optimize "git checkout -b <new_branch>", 2018-08-16).
